chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wearing furs and performing salat (prayer) in them, so he said: “Do not perform salat (prayer) in them except in that which is from what has been properly slaughtered.”
He said: I said, “Is not the properly slaughtered that which has been slaughtered with iron?” He said: “Yes, if it is from that whose flesh is eaten.”

So I said, “And what about that whose flesh is not eaten, other than sheep?” He said: “There is no harm in the squirrel, for it is a creature that does not eat meat, and it is not from that which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade, when he forbade every possessor of a fang or claw.”

key_terms.السِّنْجَابِ: squirrel, mentioned here as an exception
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.بِالْحَدِيدِ: with iron, referring to slaughter by an iron blade
key_terms.ذَكِيًّا: properly slaughtered according to the sacred law
key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: whose meat is lawful to eat

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in fur garments according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing salat (prayer) in garments made from animal fur. It states that prayer is only valid in skins from properly slaughtered animals whose meat is lawful to eat, while making an exception for squirrel on the basis that it is not among predatory animals forbidden by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
